newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit falls back vs dollar in choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit falls back vs dollar in choppy trade.

text.p: The ringgit fell back against the dollar on strong bids for the dollar/ringgit by European players, dealers said on Tuesday.
But stop-loss selling capped the dollar's rise at 2.5020/30, they said.

"Following a weak dollar/yen, the market was trying to sell down the dollar/ringgit but there was strong resilience," said a foreign bank dealer in Singapore. "There are fresh bids (for the dollar) at 2.4980/5000."
Dealers said the Malaysian unit was also pressured by selling in ringgit/Singapore dollar cross.
The ringgit had recovered from an earlier low on renewed selling of dollar/ringgit as the dollar weakened sharply against the yen.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.5000/10 a dollar at 1000 GMT against 2.4990/5000 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Monday. It traded as high as 2.4940/50 earlier.

Trading was thin throughout as players refrained from taking large positions ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) policy-setting meeting and the Buddhist Wesak Day holiday in Malaysia on Wednesday.
Dealers said foreign funds were still trying to get out of their positions and the dollar would be sold on any rallies against the ringgit.
Given the prevailing high short-term rates, it would be too expensive for players to maintain short ringgit positions, they said.
